audit.whatIsWrong: Chart reads Skill, Warwick, Warwick, Skill, Skill, Warwick, Warwick in both layers, while whys[0] says Warwick owns Level 1, whys[1], whys[2] and whys[4] say Maokai owns 2, 3 and 6, and the packet chart agrees with the prose, not the chart.
audit.why: Warwick's Level 1 is genuinely strong (Blood Hunt move speed plus Eternal Hunger on-hit healing against your single ability). From 2 your W root plus Sap Magic beats him until Jaws of the Beast is levelled and itemised.
audit.corrected: Level 1 Warwick, Levels 2-3 Maokai, Levels 4-5 Skill, Level 6 Maokai, First item and 2+ items Warwick.

audit.why: Warwick's spikes are correctly placed at first item and beyond, where Jaws of the Beast's percent-max-HP bite heals him for what it deals. Maokai spikes at 2-3 and 6.

audit.whatIsWrong: The single most useful interaction in this matchup is absent: Infinite Duress is a channelled leap, so CC applied to Warwick during it cancels the suppression. The page only says 'root/peel around it'. The mid string also carries a stray editorial aside — 'his Q (Infinite Duress is the R; his Q is the lifesteal heal)' — shipped to the reader. Primal Howl is never mentioned at all.
audit.why: Riot's kit marks Infinite Duress as a channel and it is 110/90/70s. Eternal Hunger heals him below 50% health and triples that healing below 25%, which is why brawling him low is the specific error, not 'fighting without anti-heal' generically. Primal Howl gives him 2.5s of damage reduction and a 1s flee on release — it breaks your follow-up after the root.
audit.corrected: Channel-cancel and the 110s cooldown written into dosFull[0].d and whys[4]; the aside removed from mid and replaced with the real ability names; Eternal Hunger's sub-25% tripling into dontsFull[0].d.
sources: brief enemyKit R channel flag + cd 110/90/70

audit.whatIsWrong: Maokai's Q carries a 'grounding' derived flag in the kit file, which would make Bramble Smash shut off Warwick's Q lunge and R leap — a huge claim.
audit.why: Riot's own description of Bramble Smash says only that it knocks back nearby enemies, deals magic damage and slows. Nothing about grounding. Per the rule that the description beats a derived flag, nothing about grounding was written into the page.
audit.corrected: No grounding claim made anywhere; flagged here instead.
sources: brief ownerKit Q text vs its grounding flag

edits.before: Your R (Nature's Grasp) roots him through his R-suppress engage, the one window your lockdown beats his chase.
edits.after: Nature's Grasp roots him mid-chase and CC cancels the Infinite Duress channel — the window your lockdown beats his.

edits.before: Through Levels 4-5 it evens out — your root cooldown lets you repeat short trades, but his Q (Infinite Duress is the R; his Q is the lifesteal heal) and passive lifesteal mean every extended fight refills him. Don't sit in melee trading autos; he wins attrition. At 6 your R (Nature's Grasp) is the swing: hold it to root him when he R-suppresses in, or to cancel a chase his blood-scent set up. Land that and you flip an all-in he expected to win.
edits.after: Through Levels 4-5 it evens out — your root cooldown lets you repeat short trades, but Jaws of the Beast heals him for the damage it deals and Eternal Hunger refills him under half, so every extended fight tops him up. Don't sit trading autos; he wins attrition. At 6 your R is the swing: Infinite Duress is a channelled leap and CC on him cancels it, so root him out of the suppress or wall off the chase Blood Hunt set up.

edits.before: His all-in suppress. Root/peel around it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Infinite Duress is 110s at rank 1 and channelled — any CC on him cancels it.

edits.before: That is Warwick's favourite window — refuse it and half his win condition is gone.
edits.after: Eternal Hunger's healing triples below 25% health — never brawl him low, ever.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Jaws of the Beast heals for its percent-max-HP bite — bring Grievous.

notes: Maokai's Q has a 'grounding' derived flag that Riot's own Bramble Smash text does not support; I treated the description as authoritative and made no grounding claim. If that flag is correct it would change several Maokai matchups against dash champions, so it is worth checking at champion level. Whether CC cancelling Infinite Duress requires the CC to land before the suppression applies, or also breaks it mid-suppress, is not in the kit — the text I wrote says only that CC cancels the channel.
